## Natural history notes

A slender assassin bug characterized by a narrow greenish to brown body, long legs, and a piercing beak held beneath the head. In Florida, Zelus cervicalis is found in warm gardens, fields, pine flatwoods, hammocks, forest edges, parks, and shrubby vegetation where small insect prey are common. It is a predatory true bug that stalks and ambushes flies, caterpillars, leafhoppers, and other arthropods, often using sticky forelegs to help hold prey; like other assassin bugs, it should be observed without handling because it can deliver a painful defensive bite.
